coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay School
record.summary: SFUSD's Mission Bay School is a four-story TK-5 campus at 1415 Owens St (about 81,800 sq ft per the design team; SF Standard says approximately 80,000) designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies, the design-build team SFUSD hired in 2022, under a reported $95.4 million construction contract funded by SFUSD's 2016 bond program (Proposition A). SFUSD held the ribbon cutting on August 6, 2026 and scheduled the first PreK/TK/K students for August 2026, making it Mission Bay's first public elementary school and SFUSD's first new school in about a decade.

facts.value: 1415 Owens St (site bounded by Owen Street, Nelson Rising Lane, Mission Bay Boulevard and 6th Street)
SFUSD's 2016 Proposition A school facilities bond (voter-approved)

550 students at full build-out per SFUSD (press release of August 7, 2026: "grow to a 550-student elementary school serving Pre-K through 5th grade"); SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says 'more than 400 students' and 2022 pre-construction reporting said 'up to 550' and '600' -- see open questions

Designed to be twice as sustainable as SFUSD's standard; Universal Design for Learning with movable glass partitions joining classrooms; ground-floor spaces with direct outdoor access; built-in classroom observation rooms for teacher training on each floor

A 'Mission Bay Hub' STEM program for high schoolers: SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says it draws students from six high schools; SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) says about 90 students from five high schools are enrolled this year, with capacity at 120 (the sources may count different things); described in 2022 as a STEM-focused linked learning hub preparing students for careers in health, bioscience and STEM fields, plus district professional-development space

changes.text: The 2026-09-24 row links the chair's remark to the school at 1415 Owens St and gives event date 2026-08. OCII minutes, 2026-08-18: "Chair Scott announced that she attended a ribbon-cutting event at the Mission Bay grade school near the Chase Center." The minutes name no school and no date; 2026-08 is the meeting month, and the match to this building is our inference. The earlier row is left as written.

The San Francisco Chronicle reported on August 17, 2026 that construction of the school building "wrapped up late last year"; SFUSD had scheduled completion by January 2026. The high school program on the fourth floor draws students from six high schools according to the San Francisco Standard, while the Chronicle counts about 90 students from five high schools enrolled this year. The Registry and the Chronicle put the project at about $129 million to $130 million, while the Standard reports a $95.4 million construction contract.
Mission Bay School's first day of class, August 17, 2026, is now confirmed by the San Francisco Chronicle's report of that day. The source's title is also corrected.
The Mission Bay School page now records that SFUSD says the school's land was formally transferred from UCSF to SFUSD in 2022, and gives SFUSD's own figure of 550 students at full build-out.

The Mission Bay page now says the SF Chronicle reported nearly 200 students arriving for the first day of class on Monday, August 17, 2026, instead of saying the day was upcoming. The January 2026 construction date is labeled as a scheduled date from an October 2025 SFUSD announcement; no completion report was found.
Added a photo taken on site on September 30, 2026.
Mission Bay School's opening now cites the Chronicle's first-day report of August 17, 2026, not only a preview article.

The record now gives the construction contract as about $95.4 million (SF Standard, Aug 2026) instead of $95,390,000, and says SFUSD scheduled construction to finish by January 2026 rather than stating that it was completed. The first day of school is shown as August 2026, since the readable sources give only the month. The 2022 UCSF site transfer and 1988 set-aside, the Multistudio architect credit, the Architecture 2030 claim, the attendee list at the 2022 groundbreaking and the 'first new school in 20 years' wording were removed or corrected because no cited source supports them. Sources were added for the design-build team, the Proposition A bond and the fourth-floor program.

open_questions: Full-build-out (2032) enrollment capacity is reported differently: SFUSD's August 7, 2026 press release says the school will "grow to a 550-student elementary school serving Pre-K through 5th grade", SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says more than 400 students, and 2022 pre-construction reports said up to 550 and 600. The district's own figure is 550.

Project cost is reported two ways: SF Standard (August 6, 2026) says the school "was built under a $95.4 million construction contract" (it does not name the parties; SFUSD's August 7, 2026 release names McCarthy Building Companies and DLR Group as its delivery partners), while The Registry (August 6, 2026) calls the project a "$129 million design-build effort" and the SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) "the nearly $130 million project". No source read breaks down the difference.
No SFUSD document names a square-footage figure officially; the 81,800/82,000 sq ft figures come from trade press, not the district itself.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

CORRECTED 2026-09-24: the 2032-08 grade-growth milestone (school growing one grade per year to full TK-5) was tagged with a 'planned' status, which the site's timeline read as the whole record reverting to pre-construction 'planned' status for any date past August 2032 -- even though the school is already built and open. The same error had been found on 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)', and every record was then checked for the same pattern, which found this one. That milestone describes enrollment growth, not a change in construction status, so it should never have carried a status at all; the status was removed. The milestone's date, text and sources are unchanged.

The school site's transfer: SFUSD's August 7, 2026 press release says "The land parcel was formally transferred from UCSF to SFUSD in 2022, although the plan for a school in Mission Bay has been in the works since 1998" (an event year stated by the district; no day is given). No source was found for a 1988 set-aside, so that was removed on 2026-09-29. No exact construction-completion date was found: SFUSD scheduled completion by January 2026 and the SF Chronicle (August 17, 2026) says construction wrapped up late last year; [Updated 2026-10-12: the first day of school, Monday, August 17, 2026, is now confirmed from a readable source written the same day, after the event: the SF Chronicle (Aug 17, 2026) reports "A brand-new school had opened. Nearly 200 San Francisco students poured into Mission Bay School" and describes the first day of class there.]

record.notes: Mission Bay School, 1415 Owens St (SFUSD) -- a four-story TK-5 public school (Mission Bay's first public elementary school; SF Standard calls it SFUSD's first new school in about a decade), designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies under a reported $95.4 million construction contract (SF Standard, Aug 2026). SFUSD scheduled construction to be completed by January 2026 (Oct 2025 announcement); the SF Chronicle (Aug 17, 2026) says construction wrapped up late last year, with no exact date. Ribbon cutting Aug 6, 2026; first students (pre-K/TK/K, with grades phasing in through 2032) in August 2026 (sfusd.edu; sfstandard.com).
